Suggestions of what to do if the NSO is unable to acquire scanner data
directly from retailers\

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Alternative approaches to acquiring scanner data {#Alternativeapproachestoacquiringscannerdata-Alternativeapproachestoacquiringscannerdata}

In the case that the National Statistical Office (NSO) cannot obtain
scanner data directly from the retailers, an alternative approach is to
get the data from market research companies ([CPI Manual, Concepts and
Methods](https://www.imf.org/-/media/Files/Data/CPI/cpi-manual-concepts-and-methods.ashx),
2020). Ref. (1) provides a practical example of this use case.

Usually in this kind of approach data supply will not be free and
financial resources are necessary to purchase the data. Advantages of
the approach may include the negotiation of data sets relating to
different retailers from one or a few data providers. The supply of
cleaned data already classified according to the Consumer Price Index
(CPI) classification can also be a benefit of this approach. This can
lead to reduced costs than those incurred by the NSO to build all the
infrastructure to perform all these steps on its own. 

Besides the cost for obtaining the data, other disadvantages in this
process include reduction in the control of the data being received and
the loss of flexibility in the negotiation of the data sets and
variables of interest and possible changes in data content over time.

Eurostat\'s HICP - [Practical Guide for Processing Supermarket Scanner
Data](https://circabc.europa.eu/ui/group/7b031f10-ac19-4da3-a36f-58708a70133d/library/8e1333df-ca16-40fc-bc6a-1ce1be37247c/details)
recommends whenever possible, to obtain scanner directly from the
retailers.
